title: Philippines’ Eala wins stop-start rainy affair to book Hong Kong Open final spot
text:
Philippines’ Alexandra Eala wins stop-start rainy affair to book Hong Kong Open final spot | South China Morning Post Hong Kong - Hong Kong Philippines’ Eala wins stop-start rainy affair to book Hong Kong Open final spot Advertisement WTA (Women's Tennis Association) Sport Hong Kong Philippines’ Alexandra Eala wins stop-start rainy affair to book Hong Kong Open final spot 
 Fan favourite battles over three sets to defeat Maria Sakkari of Greece to set up meeting with American Claire Liu in Sunday’s decider
 3 -MIN READ 3 -MIN Listen Mike Chan Published: 9:41pm, 7 Nov 2026 Updated: 11:16pm, 7 Nov 2026 Local fan favourite Alexandra Eala had to dig deep amid stops and starts to earn a hard-fought 7-5, 3-6, 6-4 victory over Maria Sakkari on Saturday, booking her place in the Prudential Hong Kong Tennis Open final.
 The evenly matched semi-final between the two seeded players was filled with extraordinary shots from both players, and a lot of rainwater and match suspensions.
 “I think it was just blank [during those rain stops], it took a lot of patience, but a lot, a lot, a lot of people stayed, even back in the warm-up,” said the 21-year-old Eala. “Honestly, I’m really happy that I was able to come out of that a better player.”
